title: Knowledge Layer & Governance | ContextMint Docs
description: How the Engine Knowledge tab supports governance — structural registries, activity audit, worked examples, data persistence, and screenshot checklist for operators.
lead: Governance in ContextMint answers “Is this codebase healthy?” (Quality map, DRY findings, patch gates). The Engine Knowledge tab answers “What did indexing discover, and what did the system do?” — structural facts plus a redacted activity audit. Together they give operators and leads a verifiable trail without opening JSON sidecars or VS Code.

callout.labelBefore: Where to open it: ContextMint Engine → left nav →
callout.labelAfter: (http://localhost:1420 in browser dev, or the desktop window after npm run tauri dev). Requires contextmint serve on loopback.

surfaces.title: Two surfaces — do not confuse them

rows.question: Are we duplicated / violating config policy / carrying god-files?
What routes, services, and docs did we index? Who imports whom?
Did chat use governance fast path? What was latency? Which workspace?

surfaces.footerBefore: Deep dive on patch gates and quality scans:

structure.title: Knowledge → Structure
structure.intro: After indexing, ContextMint writes Knowledge Layer sidecars under <workspace>/.contextmint/registries/ — routes, services, documents, sections, and (when extractors populate them) policies. The Structure segment is a searchable browser over those objects, not a live search over source files.

kindTabs.title: Kind tabs
items: Routes — HTTP method + path, handler file, registration hub (app/api.py), mount in main.py
Services — service symbols, definition file, consumer importers
Documents — PDF/Markdown sections indexed as document objects
Policies — governance/CI policy rules (index-time; grows as extractors ship)

structure.agreementNote: Each row shows an Agreement score (0–1) from index-time signals — similar in spirit to governance trust metadata in chat, but for structural extraction confidence.

graphPreview.title: Graph preview (right pane)
items: Route — vertical chain: mount → registration → handler → route
Service — definition card + consumer list (not one long misleading chain)
Document / file focus — focus file + imports / imported-by neighbourhood

figure.alt: Engine Knowledge tab — Routes structure list and registration graph
figure.caption: Routes: select a row to see mount → app/api.py → handler wiring.

activity.title: Knowledge → Activity
activity.intro: The Activity segment tails the server append-only audit JSONL. Events include chat streams, governance fast-path decisions, indexing milestones, ACL changes, and action confirmations — with no raw query text (privacy by design).
items: Filter by workspace, event type (e.g. governance_fast_path), and text search on metadata
Since dropdown: 15 min, 1 h, 6 h, or 24 hours — this is a view filter, not deletion
Export JSON — download redacted events for support or compliance review

figure.alt: Engine Knowledge tab — Activity audit stream with governance_fast_path events
figure.caption: Activity: prove a governed answer used the findings-store path (filter governance_fast_path).

persistence.title: Is data only kept for 24 hours?
persistence.answer: No. Persistence and the UI time window are different things.

rows.limit: Default view: last 1 hour; max dropdown: 24 hours; up to 2 000 events per request

persistence.rotationNote: Audit files rotate when a single file exceeds ~50 MB (renamed with a timestamp suffix); older lines remain on disk. ContextMint does not currently auto-delete audit JSONL by age — the 24 h cap is only what the Engine UI loads by default for responsiveness. For older history, read files under ~/.contextmint/audit/ directly or use Export JSON within the widest window.
persistence.tunablesBefore: Operator tunables: engine.audit_tail_default_since_minutes, engine.audit_tail_max_since_minutes (1440 = 24 h) in server defaults — see

example1.title: Example 1 — Verify a governed DRY answer (C4 UAT)
steps: In VS Code, ask in Repo lane: “Is any logic repeated unnecessarily in this codebase?”
Pass criteria: toast Answer from quality map; reasoning shows findings-store path.
In Engine → Knowledge → Activity, set Since to 24 hours, filter type governance_fast_path.
Confirm a new row: workspace id, latency, optional governance_path / findings metadata in exported JSON (no query text).
example1.note: Quality tab shows what was found; Activity shows that the fast path ran — together they support audit questions from security or PMO.

example2.title: Example 2 — Cross-check a config-policy finding
steps: Engine → Quality — note a config policy finding on app/services/foo.py (hardcoded timeout).
Select the service row; graph pane lists Consumers — files that import the service.
Decide blast radius before refactor: more consumers → higher governance risk for assisted apply.

figure.alt: Engine Knowledge tab — Services list with consumer graph
figure.caption: Services: consumer list supports governance triage after a Quality finding.

example3.title: Example 3 — Trust a structural chat answer (B3)
steps: VS Code Repo lane: “What route handles POST /api/v1/chat/stream?”
Answer should cite app/routers/chat.py and registration in app/api.py.
Agreement score and graph chain should match the answer. Low agreement or empty registry → reindex or investigate extractor gaps before trusting production routing questions.

example4.title: Example 4 — Document governance (handbook / ADR)
steps: Engine → Knowledge → Documents — search ADR or policy keyword.
Select a section row; graph shows file neighbourhood for where that doc lives in the repo.
Use when reconciling written policy (docs) vs code policy findings (Quality tab) — Policies kind will converge the same index-time model over time.

figure.alt: Engine Knowledge tab — Documents list with file focus graph
figure.caption: Documents: long labels are ellipsized in the table; full text in tooltip / graph pane.

screenshotChecklist.title: Screenshot checklist (for docs & carousel)
screenshotChecklist.intro: Capture at 1280px wide (dark theme). Save under contextmint-ai/src/assets/img/screenshots/ then npm run build.

rows.capture: Structure segment — workspace picker, kind tabs with counts, table + graph split
Routes tab — one API route selected; mount → api.py → handler graph visible
Services tab — definition + Consumers list (after Quality scan optional)
Documents tab — ADR or handbook row; file focus graph
Activity segment — Since = 24 hours; filter governance_fast_path; ≥1 event visible
Activity — Export JSON button + browser download or toast (optional)

beforeItems: Index your repo in VS Code; run at least one governed chat (C4 prompt) so Activity has events
Run a Quality scan so you can reference a real finding in Example 2 walkthrough

pairing.title: Pairing with VS Code governance UI
items: Governance drawer (Context Lens) — live findings during chat; Knowledge does not duplicate this
Trust chip (Governance · HIGH) — answer confidence; Activity audit proves path taken
Reasoning timeline — developer-facing; operators use Engine for aggregate proof

enterprise.title: Enterprise / compliance notes
items: Audit JSONL omits raw prompts and query text — only hashes and metadata
Export + support bundle (About tab) for incident response
ACL grant/revoke events appear in Activity when enterprise auth is enabled
